Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-2⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}=2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨0,\,-2,\,0⟩\times ⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-2\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the radius of the osculating circle at  $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}=\frac{{2}^{3}}{\,2\,}=4.\end{aligned}
$$
